gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a common 1/3 hp pump, the Zoeller M53 (9.7 A × 115 V = 1,116 W running, about 2,979 W to start), draws about 72% more than the 650 W that RunTimeFit assumed. At RunTimeFit's own 25% duty, the pick it and ChatGPT gave (PECRON F3000LFP) runs about 9 hours, not 16. Of the stations here, only the DELTA Pro 3 at about 11.8–12 h comes within reach of 12 hours at that duty.
standout_why: I compared against runtimefit.com (cited: 650 W pump, 25% duty, PECRON 16 h), testedwatts.com (cited: has the M53 at 1,116 W but only works out runtime for 1 kWh and 2 kWh stations at 2, 5 and 10 min/hr) and outagereadyhq.com (cited: 800 W pump at 5 and 20 min/hr, cost per rated Wh). None of them applies a real pump's nameplate draw to the 3–4 kWh stations they recommend. None gives the highest duty cycle each station can sustain for 12 hours. None uses a measured usable-Wh figure in place of an assumed 85%. None puts a number on a literal 13 hp load.
decides: This changes the pick. With an M53-class pump at 25% duty, the 3 kWh stations (PECRON F3000LFP and BLUETTI Elite 300) last about 9 hours, and the most duty they can hold for 12 hours is about 19%. The Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus reaches about 11.3 h. The EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the only one near 12 h (about 11.8–12 h), but it is currently unavailable. The page should lead with the highest duty each station can carry for 12 h (about 19% for 3 kWh, about 24% for 4 kWh) and tell readers to read their pump's amps off the label. Read literally, 13 hp is about 9.7 kW of shaft power, which is more than any listed portable station's continuous output (the highest here is 6,000 W). So the 13 hp answer is 'no portable station'.

findings.note: 9.7 × 115 = 1,116 W; 25.9 × 115 = 2,979 W. Tested Watts takes the 25.9 A start figure from a retailer spec table. Retailer listings found by search also give 9.7 A at 115 V for the M53.
